title: Forfeiture and the consequences of a condition
shortTitle: Forfeiture and the consequences of a condition
summary: Forfeiture occurs when a party loses a promised entitlement despite having already supplied substantial performance or incurred substantial reliance, often because a condition was not met.
notes:
The concern is the relationship between the condition’s purpose and the loss caused by enforcing it strictly. Nelson and the waiver materials consider circumstances in which a party’s conduct or the governing doctrine prevents reliance on a condition. Jacob & Youngs raises a related concern about withholding the entire contract price after substantial construction.

Avoiding forfeiture is not a universal power to disregard conditions. Determine whether the event was material to the agreed exchange, whether the condition was waived or its occurrence prevented, and what the applicable doctrine permits. The reason for relief and its limits belong in the analysis.

topics.forfeiture: The severity of lost compensation or reliance may affect the treatment of a condition.
